question: A 27-year-old woman with PCOS, BMI 28 kg/m², regular glucose tolerance test, and anovulatory infertility for 14 months has not responded to three cycles of clomiphene citrate 150 mg. What is the most appropriate next ovulation induction strategy?

answers.text: Increase clomiphene citrate to 200 mg daily for 5 days

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: 150 mg is the maximum recommended dose of clomiphene citrate. Further dose escalation is not appropriate and carries no evidence of benefit; clomiphene resistance is defined as failure at 150 mg.

answers.text: Switch to letrozole 2.5–5 mg daily on days 3–7 of cycle

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Letrozole is now considered first-line for PCOS-related anovulatory infertility (ESHRE/ASRM 2023 guidelines), producing higher ovulation and live birth rates than clomiphene. After clomiphene resistance, letrozole is the recommended next step before gonadotrophins.

answers.text: Proceed directly to IVF with controlled ovarian stimulation

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: IVF is not indicated at this stage. Several medical options remain — letrozole, then gonadotrophins, then laparoscopic ovarian drilling — before escalating to IVF.

Low-dose gonadotrophins are the third-line agent for WHO Group II anovulation, used after letrozole failure. They require intensive monitoring and carry higher OHSS and multiple pregnancy risk; letrozole is the correct next step.

overallFeedback.feedback: After clomiphene resistance (failure at 150 mg), the next step for PCOS is letrozole — it is now preferred over gonadotrophins as the second agent because of better efficacy and safety profile.

Correct. After clomiphene resistance in PCOS, letrozole (2.5–5 mg, days 3–7) is the evidence-based next step — it achieves higher live birth rates with a lower multiple pregnancy risk than gonadotrophins.
